neighbours.label: the person about to make an entrance in a scene ('when another client walked into the room', 'when you walk into a home'): the subject slot where the model expects 'walked in', as against the same people in sentences with no entrance
fire: We were halfway through dinner when my uncle walked into the kitchen.
The meeting had just started when a stranger walked into the office.
Everyone went quiet as the coach walked into the locker room.
I was reading at the counter when a customer walked into the shop.
The music stopped the moment the bride walked into the hall.
She was fixing her hair when her sister walked into the bathroom.
The kids froze when their teacher walked into the classroom.
Nobody noticed when the manager walked into the break room.
quiet: We were halfway through dinner, and my uncle told a long story.
The meeting had just started, and a stranger asked about parking.
Everyone agreed that the coach had picked the right team.
I was reading at the counter, and a customer paid in coins.
The music was chosen by the bride and her mother.
She lent her sister a dress for the party.
The kids wrote a thank-you card for their teacher.
The manager signed the forms and filed them.
